clue.text: A sultan would have one in fine leather

indicators.note: the word for one is placed in the middle of the word for fine leather

parts.note: calf is soft leather made from calfskin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remark that any sultan would own a fine leather item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sultan would have' reads as the start of a sentence, but 'A sultan' alone defines. CALIF is a variant spelling of caliph.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was a Muslim ruler, much as a sultan is, so the clue treats the titles as equivalent.

clue.text: Dance, taking drink after drink after drink

indicators.note: each word for drink follows another one in sequence
and another word for drink follows that again

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, a drink
cha is slang for tea, a drink
cha is slang for tea, a drink

explanation.surface: A dancer downing one drink after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance with a quick rhythmic step.

clue.text: She's 51 and way-out!

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: way-out means wild or unconventional, so the word and is jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman of fifty-one who is wildly unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a 'she'.

clue.text: "A woman mov'd is like a — troubled" (T. of Shrew)

definitions.text: "A woman mov'd is like a — troubled" (T. of Shrew)

parts.words: "A woman mov'd is like a — troubled" (T. of Shrew)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Katherina's final speech in The Taming of the Shrew, likening an angry woman to stirred, muddied water

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's comedy with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: In the play a woman moved to anger is compared to a muddied jet of spring water.

clue.text: Frank condemnation of Conservative policies?

parts.note: 'down with' something condemns it, so DOWN stands for condemnation
the political right is the Conservative wing

explanation.surface: A forthright attack on Tory policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frank speaks plainly and bluntly, without softening anything.

clue.text: Avoid coarse material

definitions.meaning: a strong cotton or linen canvas cloth

explanation.surface: Keeping away from rough cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to bob down out of the way, and a heavy canvas cloth shares the name.

clue.text: Fighting heavyweight from a Northern town

parts.note: warring means fighting
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer from a town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: WARRINGTON is a town in Cheshire, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large town in north-west England, between Liverpool and Manchester.

clue.text: Soldiers mounted it on obtaining a proper allowance

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the word it is written upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers mounting a horse once they got a fair allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed share or allowance, as of food.

clue.text: The little Greek is an ode-composer — so impressive

parts.note: GR is the short form of Greek

indicators.note: the words is an ode are composed, put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A small Greek boasts of being a writer of odes, very grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer' arranges IS AN ODE into ANDIOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose describes something showy and imposing, meant to impress.

clue.text: Get less light

definitions.meaning: a slender candle or wick used for lighting

explanation.surface: Being told to cut down on lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that narrows gradually towards a point thins out, and a slender candle shares the name.

clue.text: A teller — but not in a bank

definitions.text: A teller — but not in a bank

parts.words: A teller — but not in a bank
parts.note: a teller here is one who tells, reading out news on radio, rather than a bank cashier

explanation.surface: Someone called a teller who does not work behind a bank counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who reads the news tells it to listeners, a teller in the literal sense.

clue.text: Walk quietly behind an old vehicle

indicators.note: the letter for quietly comes behind, after, the vehicle

parts.note: the tram is a largely bygone form of street transport
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A pedestrian creeping softly along behind a vintage tram.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or trudge a long way.

clue.text: Making such a suit a man needs expertise

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for a man
arts are skills or crafts, a kind of expertise

explanation.surface: Advice that a man going courting needs skill to press his suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests paying suit to a lady; 'suit' is in fact a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Riders do badly, causing complaint

indicators.note: riders doing something badly signals the letters of those two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Riders performing poorly and so causing a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' is the medical sense, an ailment, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or ailment is often called a disorder, as in a digestive disorder.

clue.text: On the whole, a lot failed to understand the girl

indicators.note: the words a lot have failed, broken down into a jumble

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Many people simply couldn't understand the young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether can mean all things considered, taken overall.

clue.text: This deals with 11!

parts.note: entry 11 is the card suit with the red heart symbol; read as the organ, the branch of medicine dealing with it is meant

explanation.surface: Something that deals cards of the suit at 11.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deals' suggests dealing cards, fitting the suit at 11; it means the study of the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of medicine studies the heart and its diseases.

clue.text: Bring back control over the land

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for control is placed over the land

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
a state is a country or land

explanation.surface: Restoring authority over a country.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a former position is to reinstate them.

clue.text: Common-sense denial by American

parts.note: no is a word of denial
US means American, as in United States

explanation.surface: An American refusing to accept common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is an informal British word for practical good sense or gumption.

clue.text: Debarred and prosecuted when about to pay out

indicators.note: the word for prosecuted goes about, around, the word for pay out

parts.note: sued means took to court
to spend is to pay out money

explanation.surface: Barred and taken to court as they were about to pay up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suspended is barred from duties for a time.

clue.text: The right quarters (with furniture) are to let

parts.note: E and N are compass points, quarters of the compass
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A furnished flat on the right being offered for rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests lodgings; here it means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that is available to let can be hired out for money.

clue.text: Opposed to cutting assistance, though keen enough

indicators.note: the letter for opposed to cuts into the word for assistance

parts.note: aid is help or assistance
V is versus, meaning against or opposed to

explanation.surface: Someone against cuts to aid yet still eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager or enthusiastic about something is being avid for it.

clue.text: The medico increased the head's gloom

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
rose means went up or increased
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A doctor makes a headmaster's depression worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a headmaster; NESS is a headland, found in place names like Loch Ness's neighbours and Shoeburyness.
explanation.definitionFit: Moroseness is a sullen, gloomy mood.

clue.text: Assumes an appealing attitude

parts.note: appealing here means pleading, and the attitude a posture taken on bended knee

explanation.surface: Someone striking a charming pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down on bended knee is the posture of one making an appeal.

clue.text: Agreeable person a fool put down

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to enter is to put down or record in writing

explanation.surface: An agreeable person being insulted as a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: One who agrees or consents to a proposal is an assenter.

clue.text: A levy to be raised as appropriate

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for levy is raised, written upwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A tax to be increased when appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate funds is to set them aside, assign them.

clue.text: Walk out to impress

definitions.meaning: to make an impression on someone, as an idea striking you

explanation.surface: Leaving the room to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who walk out down tools in protest, and an idea that impresses you is said to hit you forcibly.

clue.text: Worked up a bit of a stir at every opportunity

indicators.note: only a portion of the words a stir at every is taken

explanation.surface: Someone causing a little commotion whenever possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up is being angry and agitated.

clue.text: This is about a pupil making a bloomer

definitions.meaning: the coloured ring of the eye surrounding its pupil

explanation.surface: A schoolchild making a howler.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring of the eye encircles the pupil, and a garden flower shares the name.

clue.text: Don't take a holiday

definitions.meaning: abandon or let something stay behind
time off work, as in annual vacation entitlement

explanation.surface: A worker refusing to go on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is to let it stay put rather than take it, and time off from work is also so called.

clue.text: The way the pig had swallowed a mixture of sawdust and wood-chips!

definitions.text: a mixture of sawdust and wood-chips

indicators.note: the word had takes in the other pieces as if eating them

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: How a pig gobbled up a feed of sawdust and wood shavings.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue was cut short; the page continues it.
explanation.definitionFit: This building sheet is made of compressed wood fibres, a composite of fine timber waste.

clue.text: Tears madly round, certain to get prizes

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone tearing about frantically, sure of winning prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' looks like crying but is read as rushing about; 'madly' scrambles it, and 'round' wraps the result about the word for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Things you prize, hold dear, are your valued possessions.

clue.text: Half of them tip — that's better!

indicators.note: the first half of the word them is taken

parts.note: an end or tip, the extremity of something

explanation.surface: Tipping half of them is an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it.
